name: TA-9-dsm-obstruction
why: A flat, fully-supported terrain with an above-ground DSM return (heightAboveGround) over two cells of column 2, at rows 1 and 2, both exceeding the declared obstacleHeightThreshold, forcing a detour into row 3 — pinning that obstruction blocking (not step height or NoData) is what closes these two cells. A diagonal may not cut the corner of an obstructed cell, so the moves (2,1)-(3,2) and (3,2)-(2,3) are refused; the only least-cost route (enumerated by brute force over the whole grid) is (2,0)-(3,1)-(3,2)-(3,3)-(2,4): two diagonals and two orthogonal moves, cost 2 + 2 sqrt 2.
